name: Serraleth (7-8)

source.title: Pathfinder Society Scenario #4-99: Blessings of the Forest

items.name: Disobedience Vulnerability
items.text: The first time each round an attempt to Command an Animal fails within 60 feet of Serraleth, she takes 5d6 mental damage (11d6 mental if Serraleth failed the attempt).

items.name: Predatory Aura
items.text: 30 feet. An animal or beast entering or starting its turn in the emanation must succeed at a DC 28 Will save save or become Frightened 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure). Frightened animals within the emanation can't attack Serraleth. A creature that succeeds at a saving throw against predatory aura is immune for 24 hours.

items.name: Incite Ferocity
items.text: Serraleth focuses her corruption on an animal or beast it can see within 30 feet. The creature must succeed at a DC 28 Will save save or become Confused for 1d4 rounds. The confused creature can't attack Serraleth. A creature that succeeds at its saving throw is temporarily immune to Incite Ferocity for 24 hours.

items.name: Wear Pelt
items.text: Serraleth dons the pelt of an adjacent dead animal, transforming into its lookalike. She becomes the same size and gains the same Speeds as the target animal. Serraleth loses her claw and jaws unarmed Strikes and gains the types of melee Strikes of the animal whose pelt she wears. The Strike deals damage equal to her jaws Strike or, if the Strike has the agile trait, her claw Strike. Either way, the damage type changes to match the new unarmed attack. While Serraleth wears a pelt, half of physical damage dealt to her is instead dealt to the pelt. A pelt has Hardness 5 and 25 HP. When a pelt reaches 0 HP, she's immediately expelled from the pelt and it's destroyed.

text: Rorus, sometimes called hunter demons, are brutal fiends that arise from the souls of mortals who mutilated animal corpses. As demons, these individuals don animal pelts, then infiltrate packs or herds to corrupt entire swaths of animals, turning their victims bloodthirsty and feral.
